label: n10:second-moment
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $X_1,\dots,X_n$ and $V_1,\dots,V_n$ be the generic $\bm{x}$ and $\bm{v}$ variables, respectively.
After a change of variables defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, with the corresponding dual change in the $\bm{x}$-variables, we may assume that $L=\{V_1=V_2=0\}$.
Moreover, observe that for every $\bm{v}=(0,0,\bm{v}')\in L(\mathbb{F}_q)$ we can rewrite
\[
\begin{aligned}
T_q(\bm{v})
&=\sum_{\substack{\bm{x}\in\mathbb{F}_q^n\\F(\bm{x})=0}}
  \psi_q(\bm{x}\cdot\bm{v})-q^{n-1}\bm{1}_{\bm{v}=\bm0}\\
&=\sum_{\bm{x}'\in\mathbb{F}_q^{n-2}}\psi_q(\bm{v}'\cdot\bm{x}')
  \sum_{\substack{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb{F}_q^2\\F(x_1,x_2,\bm{x}')=0}}1
  -q^{n-1}\bm{1}_{\bm{v}=\bm0}\\
&=\sum_{\bm{x}'\in\mathbb{F}_q^{n-2}}
  \bigl(\nu_F(\bm{x}')-q\bigr)\psi_q(\bm{v}'\cdot\bm{x}'),
\end{aligned}
\]
where
\[
\nu_F(\bm{x}')=\#\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb{F}_q^2:F(x_1,x_2,\bm{x}')=0\},
\]
and $\bm{x}'=(x_3,\ldots,x_n)$. Hence
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
\sum_{\substack{\bm{v}\in\mathbb{F}_q^n\\v_1=v_2=0}}|T_q(\bm{v})|^2
&=\sum_{\substack{\bm{v}\in\mathbb{F}_q^n\\v_1=v_2=0}}
\sum_{(\bm{x}',\bm{y}')\in\mathbb{F}_q^{2n-4}}
\bigl(\nu_F(\bm{x}')-q\bigr)\bigl(\nu_F(\bm{y}')-q\bigr)
\psi_q\bigl(\bm{v}'\cdot(\bm{x}'-\bm{y}')\bigr) \\
&= q^{n-2}\sum_{\bm{x}'\in\mathbb{F}_q^{n-2}} \bigl(\nu_F(\bm{x}')-q\bigr)^2,
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
by averaging over $\bm{v}$.

Since $X(\mathbb{Q})=\emptyset$, we have $F(X_1,X_2,0,\dots,0) \ne 0$,
so $\deg F(X_1,X_2,\bm{x}') = 3$ for all $\bm{x}'\in\mathbb{F}_q^{n-2}$
if $p$ is sufficiently large.
By Noether's lemma on absolute irreducibility, as in \cite[Ch.~V, Thm.~2A]{Sch76}, there exists a polynomial
$G_{F,L}(\mathbf{X}')\in\mathbb{Z}[X_3,\ldots,X_n]$ such that
\[
G_{F,L}(\bm{x}')\neq0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
F(X_1,X_2,\bm{x}')\text{ is irreducible over }\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q,
\]
for every sufficiently large prime $p$ and every $q=p^a$, where $G_{F,L}(\bm{x}')$ is evaluated in $\mathbb{F}_q$.
Moreover, $G_{F,L}$ can be chosen nonzero because the
generic specialization is absolutely irreducible,
as we show in Lemma~\ref{generic-irred} below.

For sufficiently large $p$, the reduction of $G_{F,L}$ is nonzero, so there are $O_{F,L}(q^{n-3})$ vectors $\bm{x}'\in\mathbb{F}_q^{n-2}$ at which $G_{F,L}$ vanishes.
For each such $\bm{x}'$, the polynomial $F(X_1,X_2,\bm{x}')$
has leading cubic part $F(X_1,X_2,0,\dots,0) \ne 0$,
provided that $p$ is large enough.
Thus $\nu_F(\bm{x}')\ll q$ trivially.
For the remaining vectors $\bm{x}'$, the Lang--Weil bound gives $|\nu_F(\bm{x}')-q|\ll q^{1/2}$.
Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{\bm{v}\in L(\mathbb{F}_q)}|T_q(\bm{v})|^2
&\ll_{F,L}
q^{n-2} \sum_{\substack{\bm{x}'\in\mathbb{F}_q^{n-2}\\G_{F,L}(\bm{x}')=0}} q^2
+ q^{n-2} \sum_{\substack{\bm{x}'\in\mathbb{F}_q^{n-2}\\G_{F,L}(\bm{x}')\neq0}} q \\
&\ll_{F,L}q^{2n-3},
\end{aligned}
\]
as claimed.

label: generic-irred
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $F(X_1,X_2,T_3,\dots,T_n)$ is irreducible in $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}[T_3,\dots,T_n][X_1,X_2]$,
it is irreducible in $K[X_1,X_2]$ by Gauss's lemma.
If $F(X_1,X_2,T_3,\dots,T_n)$ were reducible in $\overline{K}[X_1,X_2]$,
then by Galois theory it would have three $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)$-conjugate linear factors
$F_i = X_1+b_iX_2+c_i\in \overline{K}[X_1,X_2]$, say,
possibly after switching the variables $X_1$ and $X_2$.
Equating top-degree terms in $X_1,X_2$ gives
$F(X_1,X_2,0,\dots,0)
\in \overline{K}^\ast \prod_{i=1}^{3} (X_1+b_iX_2)$.
Factoring $F(X_1,X_2,0,\dots,0)$ over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$
gives $b_i\in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}\subset K$.
Thus $\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)$ fixes each $b_i$, whence $b_1=b_2=b_3$.
However, $X(\mathbb{Q}) = \emptyset$, so the binary cubic form
$F(X_1,X_2,0,\dots,0) \in \mathbb{Q}[X_1,X_2]$
is irreducible, and hence square-free.
This is a contradiction.
The statement of the lemma follows.

label: n10:ss-adapted
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{n10:ss-adapted}
The variety $\operatorname{\mathbb{A}}^n \setminus \{\bm0\}$ has a finite partition into smooth
homogeneous locally closed sets $C_j$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, such that
$\mathcal H^i(K_{p,\psi})$ is lisse on $C_j$
for all sufficiently large $p$
and every nontrivial $\psi$.
Moreover,
$\sum_i \operatorname{rank} \mathcal H^i(K_{p,\psi})\vert_{C_j} \ll_F 1$, uniformly over $p$ and $\psi$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cite[Theorem~2.1]{FK01}, applied to the morphism
$\widehat X\times\operatorname{\mathbb{A}}^n \to \operatorname{\mathbb{A}}^n$
in place of $X\to T$,
we obtain a finite partition $\operatorname{\mathbb{A}}^n\setminus \{\bm0\} = \bigsqcup_j Y_j$
into locally closed sets $Y_j$
such that $\mathcal H^i(K_{p,\psi})$ is lisse on $Y_j$
for all sufficiently large $p$,
and such that $\sum_i \operatorname{rank} \mathcal H^i(K_{p,\psi})\vert_{Y_j} \ll_F 1$.
The sets $Y_j$
are not necessarily smooth and homogeneous.
We modify the partition $\{Y_j\}$ as follows.

Let $V := \operatorname{\mathbb{A}}^n \setminus \{\bm0\}$.
Since $F$ is homogeneous,
the sheaves $\mathcal H^i(K_{p,\psi})$
factor through the projectivisation $V \to \operatorname{\mathbb{P}}^{n-1}$.
If $\dim Y_j = n$, then $Y_j$ contains a smooth dense open set $U_j \subset V$.
Then $\operatorname{\mathbb{G}}_m U_j\subset V$,
the union of all scalar multiples of $U_j$,
has the property that
$\mathcal H^i(K_{p,\psi})$ is lisse on $\operatorname{\mathbb{G}}_m U_j$
for all sufficiently large $p$.
This follows from gluing,
since the translates $\lambda U_j$ for $\lambda\in \operatorname{\mathbb{G}}_m$
form an open cover of $\operatorname{\mathbb{G}}_m U_j$.
Moreover, $\operatorname{\mathbb{G}}_m U_j$ is open in $V$, being a union of open sets $\lambda U_j$.

Choose $j_0$ for which $\dim Y_{j_0} = n$.
We then create a new partition of $V$
consisting of the set $C_0 = \operatorname{\mathbb{G}}_m U_{j_0}$
together with the sets $Y'_j = Y_j \setminus C_0$ for all $j$,
and let $V' := V \setminus C_0$.
Then the sets $Y'_j$ partition $V'$.
Moreover, $V'$ is homogeneous and closed in $V$.
If $\dim Y'_j$ is maximal over all $j$,
then $Y'_j$ contains a smooth open set $U'_j \subset V'$,
where $U'_j$ is dense in an irreducible component of $V'$.
Any irreducible component of $V'$ is homogeneous, so it follows that
$\mathcal H^i(K_{p,\psi})$ is lisse on $\operatorname{\mathbb{G}}_m U'_j \subset V'$
for all sufficiently large $p$.

Next, choose $j_1$ for which $\dim Y'_{j_1}$ is maximal and again let us again create a new partition of $V'$
consisting of the set $C_1 = \operatorname{\mathbb{G}}_m U'_{j_1}$
together with the sets $Y''_j = Y'_j \setminus C_1$ for all $j$,
and let $V'' := V' \setminus C_1$.
The set $V''$ is homogeneous and closed in $V'$.
Continuing in this manner,
decreasing the pair
$$(\dim V^{(r)},\text{number of top-dimensional irreducible components of }V^{(r)})$$
at each step $r\geqslant 1$,
we eventually obtain a partition
$V = \bigsqcup_{j'} C_{j'}$ into smooth homogeneous locally closed sets $C_{j'}$,
such that $\mathcal H^i(K_{p,\psi})$ is lisse on $C_{j'}$
for all sufficiently large $p$.

label: n10:moment-trace
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{n10:moment-trace}
    Let $V\subset\mathbb{A}^{n}$ be a geometrically irreducible
    affine cone of codimension $r+1$ and degree $d$, defined
    over $\mathbb{Q}$, and consider the restriction
    $K_{p,\psi}|_{V_{\mathbb{F}_p}}$.
    Let $U\subset V\setminus\{\bm0\}$ be a nonempty smooth
    open set, defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, such that, for all but
    finitely many primes $p$, the sheaves
    $\mathcal H^i(K_{p,\psi})|_{U_{\mathbb{F}_p}}$ are lisse and
    the sum of their ranks is bounded independently of $p$.
    Then either
    \[
        T_p(\bm{v})\ll_{F,V,U}p^{(n+r-2)/2}
        \qquad
        \bigl(\bm{v}\in U(\mathbb{F}_p)\bigr)
    \]
    for all sufficiently large primes $p$, or $d\geqslant r+1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a sufficiently large prime $p$.
From \eqref{eq : GLT}, we know that the restriction of
$T_{p^a}$ to $U(\mathbb{F}_{p^a})$ is an alternating sum of
trace functions of lisse sheaves that are mixed with
integer weights.
Hence, an application of
\cite[Theorem~3.5 and Remark~3.6]{Xu20}
with $w=n+r-2$ gives that either
\[
|T_{p^a}(\bm{v})|\leqslant Cp^{a(n+r-2)/2}
\qquad
\bigl(a\geqslant1,\ \bm{v}\in U(\mathbb{F}_{p^a})\bigr),
\]
where $C$ is a uniform upper bound for the sum of the
ranks in the statement, or
\[
\limsup_{a\to\infty}
\frac{1}{p^{a(2n-2)}}
\sum_{\bm{v}\in U(\mathbb{F}_{p^a})}
|T_{p^a}(\bm{v})|^2
\geqslant1,
\]
since
\[
\dim U+w+1
=(n-r-1)+(n+r-2)+1
=2n-2.
\]
In the first case, taking $a=1$ gives the desired bound.
Let us therefore assume that the second alternative holds and,
by contradiction, that $d\leqslant r$.
Consider the projective variety associated to $V$, say
$Y\subset\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$.
Since $Y$ has codimension $r+1$ in $\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ and
degree $d\leqslant r$, by applying
\cite[Lemma~3 and Corollary]{Swi73} twice, it follows that
$Y$ is contained in a linear subspace
$P\subset\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$ of codimension two.
Moreover, since $Y$ is defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, its linear span
is also defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, and we may choose $P$ to be
defined over $\mathbb{Q}$.
Let $L\subset\mathbb{A}^{n}$ be the linear subspace
associated to $P$.
Then $V\subset L$ and $\dim L=n-2$.

By Lemma~\ref{n10:second-moment}, for every $a\geqslant1$ we have
\[
\sum_{\substack{
\bm{v}\in L(\mathbb{F}_{p^a})\\
\bm{v}\ne\bm0}}
|T_{p^a}(\bm{v})|^2
\ll_{F,L}p^{a(2n-3)}.
\]
On the other hand, since
$U\subset L\setminus\{\bm0\}$, positivity gives
\[
\begin{split}
1
&\leqslant
\limsup_{a\to\infty}
\frac{1}{p^{a(2n-2)}}
\sum_{\bm{v}\in U(\mathbb{F}_{p^a})}
|T_{p^a}(\bm{v})|^2 \\
&\leqslant
\limsup_{a\to\infty}
\frac{1}{p^{a(2n-2)}}
\sum_{\substack{
\bm{v}\in L(\mathbb{F}_{p^a})\\
\bm{v}\ne\bm0}}
|T_{p^a}(\bm{v})|^2
\\
&\ll \lim_{a\rightarrow\infty} p^{-a}
\\& =0.
\end{split}
\]
This gives a contradiction.

T^{n-j-2+\varepsilon}  &\text{if $3\leqslant j\leqslant n-6$},\\

label: EQ:modified-FK-condition
title: Proof
body_md:
We start by establishing part $(i)$. Assume that
$\bm{v}\in P_j\cap\mathbb{Z}^n$, initially with
$0\leqslant j\leqslant n-6$. Fix an integer $N\geqslant1$, depending only on
$F$, such that all the chosen models and local bounds are
valid for $p\nmid N$.
By combining the bound \eqref{eq:FK-benchmark} with
Proposition \ref{n10:moment-trace}, we obtain
\[
S_p(\bm{v})\ll_F p^{\frac{n+j+1}{2}}
\]
whenever $p\nmid N$, the reduction of $\bm{v}$ is nonzero,
and
\begin{equation}
\label{EQ:modified-FK-condition}
\bm{v}\bmod p\notin
(Z_{j+1}\setminus U_{j+1})(\mathbb{F}_p).
\end{equation}

By the definition of $P_j$, either $\bm{v}\notin Z_{j+1}$
or $\bm{v}\in U_{j+1}$. In the first case, choose $g$ from
a fixed finite family of integral defining equations for
$Z_{j+1}$ such that $g(\bm{v})\ne0$. Then, for $p\nmid N$,
\[
p\nmid g(\bm{v})
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\bm{v}\bmod p\notin Z_{j+1}(\mathbb{F}_p).
\]
In the second case, $U_{j+1}$ is open in $L_{j+1}$, so
$L_{j+1}\setminus U_{j+1}$ is closed. Choose $g$ from
a fixed finite family of integral defining equations for
this complement such that $g(\bm{v})\ne0$. Since
$\bm{v}\in L_{j+1}$, its reduction belongs to
$L_{j+1}(\mathbb{F}_p)$ for $p\nmid N$. Hence
\[
p\nmid Ng(\bm{v})
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\bm{v}\bmod p\in U_{j+1}(\mathbb{F}_p).
\]
In both cases define
$\Delta(\bm{v}):=N\,|g(\bm{v})|$.
Then $p\nmid\Delta(\bm{v})$ ensures that the reduction of
$\bm{v}$ is nonzero and lies outside
$(Z_{j+1}\setminus U_{j+1})(\mathbb{F}_p)$, so the required
bound follows. Since $g$ is chosen from a fixed finite
family of polynomials depending only on $F$, we have
\[
1\leqslant\Delta(\bm{v})\ll_F(2+|\bm{v}|)^{O_F(1)}.
\]

Finally, if $j=n-5$, take
$\Delta(\bm{v}):=N|\bm{v}|$.
As noted after \eqref{eq:FK-benchmark},
Proposition~\ref{prop:prime-modulus-pointwise} then gives
\[
S_p(\bm{v})\ll_F p^{n-2}
=p^{\frac{n+j+1}{2}}
\qquad(p\nmid\Delta(\bm{v})).
\]
This completes the proof of part $(i)$.


Let us turn our attention to part $(ii)$.
When $j=0$, the
result is trivial since $P_0\subset\mathbb{Q}^n$.
Let us deal with the cases $j=1,2$. Since
$Z_j(\mathbb{Q})=R_j(\mathbb{Q})$ by \eqref{ZjRj6}, the definition
of $P_j$ gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
N(P_j,L,\bm{v}_0,m,\bm{b})
&\leqslant N\bigl(R_j\setminus(Z_{j+1}\cup U_j),L,\bm{v}_0,m,\bm{b}\bigr)
      +N(Z_{j+1},L,\bm{v}_0,m,\bm{b})\\
&=N\bigl(R_j\setminus(Z_{j+1}\cup U_j),L,\bm{v}_0,m,\bm{b}\bigr)
      +N(R_{j+1},L,\bm{v}_0,m,\bm{b}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $\operatorname{codim} R_{j+1}\geqslant j+2$,
Lemma~\ref{LEM:basically-zippel}
implies that
\[
N(R_{j+1},L,\bm{v}_0,m,\bm{b})\ll_F T^{n-j-2},
\]
which is acceptable. Let $Y$ be a geometric irreducible component
of the Zariski closure
\[
\overline{R_j\setminus(Z_{j+1}\cup U_j)}
\subset \operatorname{\mathbb{A}}^n
\]
of $R_j\setminus(Z_{j+1}\cup U_j)$ in $\operatorname{\mathbb{A}}^n$.
Based on the definition of $L_j$ and the density of $U_j$ in $L_j$
(see \eqref{n10:promotion-loci} and \eqref{n10:promotion-opens}),
we distinguish three cases.
\begin{itemize}
\item[$i)$]
The component $Y$ is defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ and has
$\deg Y\geqslant j+1$. Hence, by the uniform
Bombieri--Pila bound recorded in \cite[Theorem~A]{Pila}, we have
\[
N(Y,L,\bm{v}_0,m,\bm{b})
\ll_{F,\varepsilon}
T^{n-j-2+\frac{1}{j+1}+\varepsilon}.
\]

\item[$ii)$]
The component $Y$ is not defined over $\mathbb{Q}$. In this case,
there exists a subvariety $W\subset Y$, defined over
$\mathbb{Q}$, of codimension at least $1$ in $Y$, such that
$Y(\mathbb{Q})\subset W(\mathbb{Q})$. Hence,
by Lemma~\ref{LEM:basically-zippel},
we have
\[
N(Y,L,\bm{v}_0,m,\bm{b})
\ll_F T^{n-j-2}.
\]

\item[$iii)$]
The component $Y$ has $\deg Y\leqslant j$ and is defined over $\mathbb{Q}$.
Then necessarily $\dim Y\leqslant n-j-2$,
or else $Y$ would be contained in $L_j$ by \eqref{n10:promotion-loci}.
Hence,
by Lemma~\ref{LEM:basically-zippel},
we have
\[
N(Y,L,\bm{v}_0,m,\bm{b})
\ll_F T^{n-j-2}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Summing over the finitely many components, the bound follows.
For $3\leqslant j\leqslant n-6$, the argument is almost the same, except
for the treatment of the geometrically irreducible components
of
\[
\overline{R_j\setminus(Z_{j+1}\cup U_j)}
\]
that are defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ and have degree at least
$j+1\geqslant4$. If $Y$ is such a component, then we have
\[
N(Y,L,\bm{v}_0,m,\bm{b})
\ll_{F,\varepsilon} T^{n-j-2+\varepsilon},
\]
by \cite[Theorem~1.2]{Vermeulen}, provided that $Y$ is not
cylindrical over a curve.

We claim that $Y$ is not cylindrical over a curve. Since
$R_j$, $Z_{j+1}$ and $U_j$ are homogeneous, $Y$ is an affine
cone associated to a projective variety. Put $r:=\dim Y$.
If $Y$ were cylindrical over a curve, there would exist a
surjective $\mathbb{Q}$-linear map
\[
\pi:\operatorname{\mathbb{A}}^n\longrightarrow\operatorname{\mathbb{A}}^{n-r+1}
\]
and an affine curve $C$ such that $Y=\pi^{-1}(C)$.
Since $\pi$ is linear and $Y$ is homogeneous, $C$ is also
homogeneous. Moreover, $C$ is geometrically irreducible,
since $Y$ is geometrically irreducible. Hence $C$ must be
a line. It follows that $Y=\pi^{-1}(C)$ is a linear space,
contradicting $\deg Y\geqslant4$.
The case $j=n-5$ follows from the fact that $R_{n-5}$ has dimension $\leqslant 1$ and $R_{n-4}=\{\mathbf 0\}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathcal L$ be the left-hand side of \eqref{n10:weighted-mean-comp}.
As in the proof of Lemma~\ref{n10:weighted-conductor}, write
\[
r=R_{j+2,k+2}(d,\bm{v}),\qquad c=\gcd(d,r^2),\qquad b=d/c.
\]
Then $\operatorname{rad}(c)=r\geqslant T$, $\gcd(b,c)=1$ and
$R_{j+2,k+2}(b,\bm{v})=1$.
For $j+2\leqslant h\leqslant n-4$, let $c_h$ be the product of all prime powers
$p^\nu\parallel c$ of depth $h$, where the depth of a prime power is defined to be
$e(\bm{v};p)$ if $\nu=1$
and $f(\bm{v};p)$ if $\nu=2$.
Put $r_h=\operatorname{rad}(c_h)$.
Then
\[
c=\prod_hc_h,\qquad r=\prod_hr_h\geqslant T,\qquad
r_h\leqslant c_h\leqslant r_h^2,\qquad c\leqslant2D.
\]
If $c=d_1d_2^2$, then \eqref{EQ:K-relaxed-hybrid-pointwise} gives
$$\frac{S_c(\bm{v})}{c^{(n+j+3)/2}}
\ll (DH)^\varepsilon d_2^{k-j} K(d_1d_2^2,\bm{v})
\leqslant (DH)^\varepsilon \prod_{h=j+2}^{n-4}c_h^{(h-j-2)/2},$$
by the definition of $K(d_1d_2^2,\bm{v})$ in \eqref{n10:K},
since $k\geqslant j$.
Yet for fixed $c,\bm{v}$,
we have
$$\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{cube\text{-}free}\ b\sim D/c \\ R_{j+2,k+2}(b,\bm{v})=1}}
|S_b(\bm{v})| \ll (DH)^\varepsilon (D/c)^{(n+j+3)/2},
$$
by \eqref{eq:fix-cv}.
Therefore,
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal L
\ll \sum_{c_h,r_h}
\sum_{\substack{
\bm{v}\in(P_j\cap Q_k)\cap\mathcal V\\
\bm{v}\bmod{r_h} \in Z_h(\mathbb{Z}/r_h\mathbb{Z})}}
(DH)^\varepsilon D^{(n+j+3)/2} \prod_{h=j+2}^{n-4}c_h^{(h-j-2)/2}.
\end{equation*}
Let $\mathcal L'$ be the contribution from $c_h\sim C_h$ and $r_h\sim R_h$.
Then $\mathcal L' = 0$ unless
\[
\prod_h C_h\ll D,\qquad
\prod_h R_h\gg T,\qquad R_h\ll C_h\ll R_h^2.
\]
For fixed $r_h$, there are at most
$2^{\omega(r_h)}\ll_\varepsilon D^\varepsilon$ possible choices for $c_h$.
Hence
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal L'
\ll \mathcal N(\bm R)
(DH)^\varepsilon D^{(n+j+3)/2} \prod_{h=j+2}^{n-4} C_h^{(h-j-2)/2},
\end{equation*}
where $\mathcal N(\bm R)$ is the quantity in
Proposition~\ref{lem:stratified-composite-sieve}
with $Y_0=\operatorname{\mathbb{A}}_\mathbb{Z}^n$,
$\mathcal U=(P_j\cap Q_k)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n$,
$Y_i = Z_{j+1+i}$ for $1\leqslant i\leqslant s=n-5-j$,
and with dyadic parameters $R_{j+1+i}$ in place of $R_i$.
Indeed, the set $\mathcal U$
lies outside all the varieties $Z_h$
with $h\geqslant j+2$.
In fact, $P_j \cap Z_{j+2} = \emptyset$ by \eqref{n10:rational-partition},
since $U_{j+1} \cap Z_{j+2} = \emptyset$ by \eqref{n10:promotion-opens}.

By \eqref{n10:progression-counts},
the hypothesis \eqref{eq:stratified-progression-hypothesis}
of Proposition~\ref{lem:stratified-composite-sieve}
certainly holds with $\alpha = n-j$.
Moreover, \eqref{eq:silver} yields $\dim Z_h \leqslant f(h)$, where $f(h) := n-h-\delta_{n-5,n-4}(h)$.
Since $f$ is (strictly) decreasing on the interval $j+2\leqslant h\leqslant n-4$,
Proposition~\ref{lem:stratified-composite-sieve} implies that
\[
\mathcal N(\bm R) \ll_{F,\varepsilon}(DH)^\varepsilon\Biggl(
1+\frac{T^{n-j}}{\prod_{h=j+2}^{n-4}R_h^{n-j-f(h)-1}}
+\sum_{\ell=j+2}^{n-4}
\frac{T^{f(\ell)+1}}
 {\prod_{h>\ell}R_h^{f(\ell)-f(h)}}
\Biggr).
\]
Let $A_0$ be the middle term in the parentheses,
and let $A_\ell$ be the summand indexed by $\ell$.
Then
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal L'
\ll A (DH)^\varepsilon D^{(n+j+3)/2} \prod_{h=j+2}^{n-4} C_h^{(h-j-2)/2},
\end{equation*}
for some $A\in \{1, A_0, A_\ell\}$.
If $A=1$, then using $\prod_h C_h\ll D$ we find that
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal L'
\ll (DH)^\varepsilon D^{(n+j+3)/2} D^{(n-4-j-2)/2}
= (DH)^\varepsilon D^{n-3/2}
\ll (DH)^\varepsilon T^4 D^{n-3/2},
\end{equation*}
which is the $\ell=n-4$ term of \eqref{n10:weighted-mean-comp}.
If $A=A_0$, then using $C_h\ll R_h^2$ we find that
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal L'
\ll (DH)^\varepsilon D^{(n+j+3)/2} T^{n-j} \prod_{h=j+2}^{n-4}
\frac{R_h^{h-j-2}}{R_h^{n-j-f(h)-1}}.
\end{equation*}
The product over $h$ equals
$\prod_{h=j+2}^{n-4} R_h^{-1-\delta_{n-5,n-4}(h)}
\ll T^{-1-\delta_{n-5,n-4}(j+2)}$,
since $\prod_h R_h\gg T$
and $\delta_{n-5,n-4}(h) \geqslant \delta_{n-5,n-4}(j+2)$ for all $j+2\leqslant h\leqslant n-4$.
Thus
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal L'
\ll (DH)^\varepsilon D^{(n+j+3)/2} T^{n-j-1-\delta_{n-5,n-4}(j+2)},
\end{equation*}
which is the $\ell=j+2$ term of \eqref{n10:weighted-mean-comp}.
Finally, suppose $A=A_\ell$, where $j+2\leqslant\ell\leqslant n-4$.
Then
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal L'
\ll (DH)^\varepsilon D^{(n+j+3)/2} T^{f(\ell)+1}
\prod_{h=j+2}^{\ell} C_h^{(h-j-2)/2}
\prod_{h=\ell+1}^{n-4} \frac{C_h^{(h-j-2)/2}}{R_h^{f(\ell)-f(h)}}.
\end{equation*}
Here $C_h^{(h-j-2)/2} \ll C_h^{(\ell-j-2)/2}$ for $h\leqslant \ell$.
Also, $R_h^{f(\ell)-f(h)} \gg R_h^{h-\ell} \gg C_h^{(h-\ell)/2}$ for $\ell < h\leqslant n-4$,
since $f$ is strictly decreasing on this interval.
It follows that
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal L'
\ll (DH)^\varepsilon D^{(n+j+3)/2} T^{f(\ell)+1}
\prod_{h=j+2}^{n-4} C_h^{(\ell-j-2)/2}
\ll (DH)^\varepsilon D^{(n+\ell+1)/2} T^{f(\ell)+1}
\end{equation*}
since $\prod_h C_h\ll D$.
This matches the $\ell$ term of \eqref{n10:weighted-mean-comp}, and so we are done.

as in \eqref{eq:q-buw-rec}. Put
\[
H_{g,r}:=2+|\bm{v}_0|+L+m_{g,r},
\]
and, for every $\bm{a}\bmod m_{g,r}$, define
\[
P_{g,r}(\bm{a})
:=
\sup_{\substack{\bm{v}\in\mathcal V\\
\bm{v}\equiv\bm{a}\bmod m_{g,r}}}
|S_{g,W_\eta}(\bm{v})S_r(\bm{v})|,
\]
with the convention that the supremum is zero if the
set is empty.
An application of Proposition~\ref{prop:n10-weighted-cube-free}
gives
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:n10-cube-free-applied}
\sum_{\substack{d\sim D\ \mathrm{cube\text{-}free}\\
\gcd(d,m_{g,r})=1}}
\sum_{\bm{v}\in\mathcal V}
w_{g,r}(\bm{v})|S_d(\bm{v})|
\ll_{F,\varepsilon} (DH_{g,r})^\varepsilon \left(\min\{\mathcal R_1, \mathcal R_2\} + \mathcal R_3\right)
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
\mathcal R_1
&= (D^{19/2}T_{g,r}+D^{41/6}T_{g,r}^{9}) \|P_{g,r}\|_1, \\
\mathcal R_2
&= D^9\|w_{g,r}\|_1, \\
\mathcal R_3
&= D^{13/2}T_{g,r}^{20/3}
\|P_{g,r}\|_1^{2/3}
\|w_{g,r}\|_1^{1/3}.
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
Here $\operatorname{rad}(m_{g,r})=\operatorname{rad}(gr)$, so that
$\gcd(d,m_{g,r})=1$ is equivalent to $\gcd(d,gr)=1$.

In order to further average the estimate \eqref{eq:n10-cube-free-applied}
over $g$ and $r$,
our strategy will be to bound
\begin{equation}
\label{EQ:mixed-endpoint-task-list}
\sum_{g\sim G}\sum_{r\sim C}\|w_{g,r}\|_1
\quad\text{and}\quad
\sum_{g\sim G}\sum_{r\sim C}
T_{g,r}^{\alpha}\|P_{g,r}\|_1
\qquad(\alpha=1,9,10)
\end{equation}
first, before attacking $\min\{\mathcal R_1,\mathcal R_2\}$
and $\mathcal R_3$ by interpolation.
We start with the average of $\|w_{g,r}\|_1$.
It will be convenient to handle the $g$-aspect using a pointwise bound.
By \eqref{fixed-p-adic-stationary-phase}, together with
Lemma~\ref{lem:inel-high-rank-point} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:restricted-multiplicative}, we have
$S_{g,W_\eta}(\bm{v})\ll_{F,\eta}g^7$
uniformly in $\bm{v}$.
Moreover, since $\mathcal P_\eta$ is fixed and finite,
there are $O_{F,\eta,\varepsilon}(G^\varepsilon)$ possible integers
$g\sim G$. Hence, for every $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{g\sim G}\sum_{r\sim C}\|w_{g,r}\|_1
&=
\sum_{g\sim G}\sum_{r\sim C}
\sum_{\bm{v}\in\mathcal V}
|S_{g,W_\eta}(\bm{v})S_r(\bm{v})|\\
&\ll_{F,\eta,\varepsilon}
G^{7+\varepsilon}
\sum_{r\sim C}\sum_{\bm{v}\in\mathcal V}
|S_r(\bm{v})|\\
&\ll_{F,\eta,\varepsilon}
G^{7+\varepsilon}C^{32/5+\varepsilon}(L+C^{1/3})^{10}\\
&\ll_{F,\eta,\varepsilon}
G^{7+\varepsilon}C^{32/5+\varepsilon}Q^{10/3}.
\end{split}
\]
Here the penultimate step follows from 
 \eqref{eq:cubefull-average-sharp} in Lemma~\ref{Le: Cubefull.finalbound}, and the
last step uses $L\leqslant Q^{1/3}$ and $C\ll Q$.

Let us focus on the other term in \eqref{EQ:mixed-endpoint-task-list},
involving the moments of $\|P_{g,r}\|_1$.
All implied constants below may depend on
$F,\eta,\varepsilon$.
Observe that \eqref{eq:Pgr} gives
\[
\|P_{g,r}\|_1
\ll
G^{28/3}r^{10+\eta}\kappa(r).
\]
Moreover, $r=b^3z_1z_2^2$ by \eqref{eq:q-buw-rec}, so we have
\[
A_g\asymp_{F,\eta}g^{1/3},
\qquad
A_r^3=b^3z_2^3 = r\frac{z_2}{z_1}=\frac{r}{u(r)^3},
\qquad
u(r):=\left(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\right)^{1/3}.
\]
Since $L\leqslant Q^{1/3}$ and $GDC\asymp Q$, we obtain
\[
T_{g,r}
\ll
1+\left(\frac{Q}{gr}\right)^{1/3}u(r)
\ll
1+D^{1/3}u(r).
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:n10-cubefull-weights}, applied with
exponents $0$ and $\alpha$, gives, for
$\alpha\in\{1,9,10\}$,
\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{g\sim G}\sum_{r\sim C}
T_{g,r}^{\alpha}\|P_{g,r}\|_1
&\ll
G^{28/3+\varepsilon}C^{10+\eta}
\left(
\sum_{r\sim C}\kappa(r)
+
D^{\alpha/3}
\sum_{r\sim C}\kappa(r)u(r)^\alpha
\right)\\
&\ll
D^{\alpha/3}G^{28/3+\varepsilon}
C^{10+\max\{0,(\alpha-9)/12\}+\eta+\varepsilon}\\
&\ll
Q^\varepsilon D^{\alpha/3}G^{28/3}
C^{10+\max\{0,(\alpha-9)/12\}+\eta}.
\end{split}
\]
Here we used $D,C\geqslant 1/2$ to absorb the contribution
of the exponent $0$, and $GC\ll Q$ in the last step.
Likewise, the preceding estimate for the weight norms
gives
\[
\sum_{g\sim G}\sum_{r\sim C}\|w_{g,r}\|_1
\ll
Q^\varepsilon G^7C^{32/5}Q^{10/3}.
\]

We are now ready to sum the bound in
\eqref{eq:n10-cube-free-applied}.
First, the moment estimates with $\alpha=1,9$ give
\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{g\sim G}\sum_{r\sim C} \mathcal R_1
&=\sum_{g\sim G}\sum_{r\sim C}
\bigl(D^{19/2}T_{g,r}
+D^{41/6}T_{g,r}^{9}\bigr)
\|P_{g,r}\|_1\\
&\ll
Q^\varepsilon
\bigl(D^{19/2+1/3}+D^{41/6+3}\bigr)
G^{28/3}C^{10+\eta}\\
&\ll
Q^\varepsilon D^{59/6}G^{28/3}C^{10+\eta}\\
&\asymp
Q^{10+\varepsilon}C^\eta D^{-1/6}G^{-2/3},
\end{split}
\]
since $GDC\asymp Q$.
On the other hand, the estimate for $\|w_{g,r}\|_1$ gives
\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{g\sim G}\sum_{r\sim C} \mathcal R_2
&\ll
Q^\varepsilon D^9G^7C^{32/5}Q^{10/3}\\
&\ll
Q^\varepsilon D^9G^7C^{13/2}Q^{10/3}\\
&\asymp
Q^{10-1/6+\varepsilon}G^{1/2}D^{5/2}.
\end{split}
\]
Since the sum of the minima $\min\{\mathcal R_1,\mathcal R_2\}$
is at most the minimum
of the sums, we obtain
\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{g\sim G}\sum_{r\sim C}
\min\{\mathcal R_1,\mathcal R_2\}
&\ll
\bigl(Q^{10+\varepsilon}C^\eta D^{-1/6}G^{-2/3}\bigr)^{15/16}
\bigl(Q^{10-1/6+\varepsilon}G^{1/2}D^{5/2}\bigr)^{1/16}\\
&=
Q^{10-1/96+\varepsilon}G^{-19/32}C^{15\eta/16}.
\end{split}
\]

It remains to bound the last term in
\eqref{eq:n10-cube-free-applied}.
By H\"older's inequality,
\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{g\sim G}\sum_{r\sim C} \mathcal R_3
&= D^{13/2}
\sum_{g\sim G}\sum_{r\sim C}
T_{g,r}^{20/3}
\|P_{g,r}\|_1^{2/3}
\|w_{g,r}\|_1^{1/3}\\
&\leqslant
D^{13/2}
\left(
\sum_{g\sim G}\sum_{r\sim C}
T_{g,r}^{10}\|P_{g,r}\|_1
\right)^{2/3}
\left(
\sum_{g\sim G}\sum_{r\sim C}
\|w_{g,r}\|_1
\right)^{1/3}\\
&\ll
Q^\varepsilon D^{13/2}
\bigl(D^{10/3}G^{28/3}C^{10+1/12+\eta}\bigr)^{2/3}
\bigl(G^7C^{32/5}Q^{10/3}\bigr)^{1/3}\\
&\asymp
Q^{10-1/30+\varepsilon}
G^{-3/10}D^{-2/15}C^{2\eta/3}.
\end{split}
\]
Here the last step uses $GDC\asymp Q$.

Since $G,D\geqslant1/2$, $C\ll Q$, and $1/30>1/96$,
both contributions are
\[
\ll Q^{10-1/96+\eta+\varepsilon}.
\]
Moreover, $m_{g,r}\mid gr$, so
$m_{g,r}\ll Q$ and $H_{g,r} \ll Q + |\bm{v}_0|$.
Restoring the factors $(DH_{g,r})^\varepsilon$ from
\eqref{eq:n10-cube-free-applied}, summing over the
$O((1+\log Q)^3)$ dyadic blocks, and rescaling $\varepsilon$,
we therefore obtain
\[
\sum_{q\sim Q}
\sum_{\substack{\bm0\ne\bm{v}\in\mathbb{Z}^{10}\\
|\bm{v}-\bm{v}_0|\leqslant L}}
|S_{q,W_\eta}(\bm{v})|
\ll_{F,\eta,\varepsilon}
(LQ+|\bm{v}_0|)^\varepsilon Q^{10-1/96+\eta}
\qquad
(L\leqslant Q^{1/3}).
\]
We now fix $0<\eta<1/96-\gamma$, depending only on
$\gamma$, and set $W=W_\eta$.
We conclude that
\[
\sum_{q\sim Q}
\sum_{\substack{\bm0\ne\bm{v}\in\mathbb{Z}^{10}\\
|\bm{v}-\bm{v}_0|\leqslant L}}
|S_{q,W}(\bm{v})|
\ll_{F,\gamma,\varepsilon}
(LQ+|\bm{v}_0|)^\varepsilon Q^{10-\gamma}
\qquad
(L\leqslant Q^{1/3}).
\]

If instead $L>Q^{1/3}$, cover the original box by
\[
O\left(\left(1+\frac{L}{Q^{1/3}}\right)^{10}\right)
\]
boxes of radius $Q^{1/3}$, with centres of size
$O(|\bm{v}_0|+L)$. Applying the preceding bound to each box,
and rescaling $\varepsilon$ if necessary, gives
\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{q\sim Q}
\sum_{\substack{\bm0\ne\bm{v}\in\mathbb{Z}^{10}\\
|\bm{v}-\bm{v}_0|\leqslant L}}
|S_{q,W}(\bm{v})|
&\ll_{F,\gamma,\varepsilon}
(LQ+|\bm{v}_0|)^\varepsilon
\left(1+\frac{L}{Q^{1/3}}\right)^{10}
Q^{10-\gamma}\\
&=
(LQ+|\bm{v}_0|)^\varepsilon
(L+Q^{1/3})^{10}Q^{20/3-\gamma}.
\end{split}
\]
Together with the case $L\leqslant Q^{1/3}$, this proves
Proposition~\ref{prop:n10-clean-shifted}.

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:gradient-volume}
Let $q\asymp_W R$, $|\theta|\sim \phi$, and let $V_0$ be given by \eqref{eq:V}.
Assume that \eqref{eq:diffU} holds.
Then, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every
$\bm{v}\in \mathbb{R}^n$, we have
\[

\bm{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n:
|\bm{x}/P-\bm{x}_0|\leqslant 2\ell,\;
|q\theta\nabla F(\bm{x})-\bm{v}|\leqslant P^\varepsilon V_0
\right\}
\ll
P^{n+O_n(\varepsilon)}\left(\frac{R}{PV_0}\right)^{\rho},
\]
where $\rho=r(F)$.

head: environment

label: aislop
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: choose-shifted box-max-vector-a
title: Proof
body_md:
For each $\bm{v}$
for which the set in the supremum is nonempty,
choose $\bm{a}=\bm{a}(\bm{v})$
with $0<|\bm{a}|\leqslant P^\varepsilon V$
and $|\bm{a}-\bm{v}| \leqslant L$
such that
\begin{equation}
\label{choose-shifted box-max-vector-a}
M_\alpha(\bm{v},L) =
\operatorname{Vol}\left\{
\bm{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n:
|\bm{x}/P-\bm{x}_0|\leqslant 2\ell,\;
|\alpha\nabla F(\bm{x})-\bm{a}|\leqslant P^\varepsilon V_0
\right\}.
\end{equation}
In particular, the outer sum is zero unless $P^\varepsilon V \geqslant 1$, which we now assume.
We begin as in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem:gradient-volume} by writing $\bm{x}=P\bm{y}$,
where $\bm{y}\in U$ by \eqref{eq:diffU}.
By the discussion after \eqref{eq:Psi},
we have a diffeomorphism
\begin{equation}
\label{key-diffeomorphism}
U\xrightarrow{\cong} S\subset \mathbb{R}^n, \quad 
\bm{y} \mapsto \left(\Psi(\bm{y}),y_{\rho+1},\dots,y_n\right),
\end{equation}
for which the Jacobian and the  Jacobian of the inverse map are uniformly bounded on $U$.
Then, for all vectors $\bm{s},\bm{t}\in \mathbb{R}^\rho$ and $\bm{y}''\in \mathbb{R}^{n-\rho}$
with $(\bm{s},\bm{y}''),(\bm{t},\bm{y}'')\in U$, we have
\begin{align}
|\nabla F(\bm{s},\bm{y}'') - \nabla F(\bm{t},\bm{y}'')|
&\ll_U |\bm{s}-\bm{t}|,
\label{easy-grad-smooth} \\
|\Psi(\bm{s},\bm{y}'') - \Psi(\bm{t},\bm{y}'')|
&\gg_U |\bm{s}-\bm{t}|.
\label{inverse-lipschitz-Psi}
\end{align}
The inequality \eqref{easy-grad-smooth} is a general consequence of the smoothness of $\nabla F$;
the inequality \eqref{inverse-lipschitz-Psi} similarly follows from the smoothness of the inverse of the diffeomorphism \eqref{key-diffeomorphism}.

Let us write $\bm{v}=(\bm{v}',\bm{v}'')$
and $\bm{a}=(\bm{a}',\bm{a}'')$
for $\bm{v}',\bm{a}'\in \mathbb{Z}^\rho$ and $\bm{v}'',\bm{a}''\in \mathbb{Z}^{n-\rho}$.
Similarly write $\bm{y}=(\bm{y}',\bm{y}'')$,
where $\bm{y}'\in \mathbb{R}^\rho$ and $\bm{y}''\in \mathbb{R}^{n-\rho}$.
By the triangle inequality
$$|\alpha\nabla F(\bm{x})-\bm{v}|
\leqslant |\alpha\nabla F(\bm{x})-\bm{a}| + |\bm{a}-\bm{v}|
\leqslant P^\varepsilon V_0 + L$$
and the change of coordinates $\bm{x}=P\bm{y}$,
\begin{equation}
\label{drop-L-box}
\operatorname{Vol}\left\{
\bm{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n:
\bm{x}/P\in U,\;
|\alpha\nabla F(\bm{x})-\bm{a}|\leqslant P^\varepsilon V_0
\right\}
\leqslant P^n \int_{\substack{\bm{y}\in U\\
|\alpha P^2\Psi(\bm{y})-\bm{a}'|\leqslant P^\varepsilon V_0}}
\bm{1}_{A(\bm{y},\bm{v})}\,
\mathrm{d}\bm{y},
\end{equation}
where $A(\bm{y},\bm{v})$ denotes the condition that
$|\alpha P^2 \frac{\partial F(\bm{y})}{\partial y_j}  
-v_j|\leqslant P^\varepsilon V_0 + L$ for $1\leqslant j\leqslant n$.
The condition $A(\bm{y},\bm{v})$ constrains $\bm{v}$ directly,
rather than $\bm{a}$,
at the cost of introducing a summand $L$.
If $\bm{v}'$ and $\bm{y}''$ are fixed,
then any two possible choices $\bm{s},\bm{t}\in \mathbb{R}^\rho$ for the vector
$\bm{y}'$ satisfy $$|\bm{s}-\bm{t}|\ll_U \frac{P^\varepsilon V_0 + L}{|\alpha P^2|},$$
by $A(\bm{y},\bm{v})$ applied with $1\leqslant j\leqslant \rho$,
together with the inequality \eqref{inverse-lipschitz-Psi}.
Then, \eqref{easy-grad-smooth} and
the case $\rho+1\leqslant j\leqslant n$ of $A(\bm{y},\bm{v})$
constrain the vector $\bm{v}''$ to lie in a box
$B(\bm{v}',\bm{y}'')$
of diameter
$$\ll_U \sup_{\bm{s},\bm{t}} |\alpha P^2| |\bm{s}-\bm{t}|
+ P^\varepsilon V_0 + L
\ll_U |\alpha P^2| \frac{P^\varepsilon V_0 + L}{|\alpha P^2|}
+ P^\varepsilon V_0 + L
\asymp P^\varepsilon V_0 + L.$$
The strategy is now to
choose $\bm{v}'$, $\bm{y}''$, $\bm{v}''$ and $\bm{y}'$ in that order,
where $$|\bm{v}'|\leqslant |\bm{v}|\leqslant |\bm{a}| + |\bm{v}-\bm{a}| \leqslant P^\varepsilon V + L.$$
Plugging \eqref{drop-L-box} into \eqref{choose-shifted box-max-vector-a}
and summing over $\bm{v}$,
it follows from our analysis of $\bm{v}'$ and $\bm{v}''$ above that
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}
\sum_{\bm{v}\in \mathbb{Z}^n}
M_\alpha(\bm{v},L)
&\leqslant P^n \sum_{\bm{v}\in \mathbb{Z}^n} \int_{\substack{\bm{y}\in U\\
|\alpha P^2\Psi(\bm{y})-\bm{a}'|\leqslant P^\varepsilon V_0}}
\bm{1}_{|\bm{v}'| \leqslant P^\varepsilon V + L}
\bm{1}_{\bm{v}''\in B(\bm{v}',\bm{y}'')}\,
\mathrm{d}\bm{y} \\
&= P^n \sum_{\substack{\bm{v}'\in \mathbb{Z}^\rho\\ 
|\bm{v}'|\leqslant P^\varepsilon V + L}}
\int_{\substack{\bm{y}''\in \mathbb{R}^{n-\rho}\\ |\bm{y}''|\ll_U 1}}
\sum_{\bm{v}''\in B(\bm{v}',\bm{y}'')}
\int_{\substack{\bm{y}'\in \mathbb{R}^\rho\\ \bm{y}\in U\\
|\alpha P^2\Psi(\bm{y})-\bm{a}'|\leqslant P^\varepsilon V_0}}
\mathrm{d}\bm{y}'\, \mathrm{d}\bm{y}'',
\end{split}
\end{equation*}
by Fubini's theorem.
For any fixed $\bm{v}'$, $\bm{y}''$ and $\bm{v}''$, the inner volume is 
$$
\ll_U P^{O_n(\varepsilon)} \min\left\{1, \frac{ V_0}{R\phi P^2}\right\}^\rho,
$$
arguing via the diffeomorphism \eqref{key-diffeomorphism}
as in the proof of \eqref{preslop}.
The number of available vectors $\bm{v}'$ and $\bm{v}''$
being $O((1+P^\varepsilon V + L)^\rho)$ and $O((1+P^\varepsilon V_0 + L)^{n-\rho})$, respectively, we get
\begin{equation*}
\sum_{\bm{v}\in \mathbb{Z}^n}
M_\alpha(\bm{v},L)
\ll P^{n+O_n(\varepsilon)} (V + L)^\rho (1+V_0+L)^{n-\rho}
\min\left\{1, \frac{ V_0}{R\phi P^2}\right\}^\rho,
\end{equation*}
since $P^\varepsilon V\geqslant 1$.

If $\phi P^3\leqslant 1$ then $V=V_0=RP^{-1}$ and the overall bound is clearly
$O(P^{n+O_n(\varepsilon)} (V+L)^n)$,
since $P^\varepsilon V\geqslant 1$.
On the other hand, if 
 $\phi P^3>1$ then $V=R\phi P^2$ and
 $V_0=R\phi^{1/2}P^{1/2}$. But then
 $V_0/(R\phi P^2)=(\phi P^3)^{-1/2}< 1$, leading to the overall  contribution
$$
\ll P^{n+O_n(\varepsilon)} (V+L)^\rho (1+V_0+L)^{n-\rho} (V_0/V)^\rho
= P^{n+O_n(\varepsilon)} (1+\tfrac{L}{V})^\rho (1+V_0+L)^{n-\rho} V_0^\rho,
$$ 
as required.

label: app:ss:lem:reduction
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{app:ss:lem:reduction}
If $t\geqslant0$
and $G_h^i(\mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ is an isomorphism for all $i>t$, then,
for $\bm{v}\neq\bm0$ with $[\bm{v}]=h$,
\[
 T_q(\bm{v})\ll_{n,d} q^{t/2}.

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In \eqref{app:ss:eq:trace}, the terms with $i>t$ vanish, since by assumption $G^i_h(\mathbb{Q}_\ell)$ is a Galois-equivariant isomorphism for $i>t$.
Deligne's general form of the Riemann hypothesis \cite[Th\'eor\`eme 3.3.1]{Del} bounds the
absolute values of the eigenvalues of the nonzero terms by
$q^{i/2}\leqslant q^{t/2}$.
Katz's bounds~\cite[Theorem~3 and its corollary]{KatzBetti}
bound the total Betti numbers of $X$ and $X_h$ in terms of $n,d$:
they are cut out by at most two equations of degree at most $d$.
The triangle inequality in \eqref{app:ss:eq:trace}
therefore gives the desired bound for $T_q(\bm{v})$.

title: Proof

We apply \cite[Theorem~1.2 and its proof]{RS} to
the inclusion morphism $\phi:X\hookrightarrow P$,
with parameters $r=\dim(X\times_P X)=\dim X=n-2$, $c=i$ and $q=a$.
The construction in \cite[Theorem~2.2, Corollary~2.3 and their proofs]{RS} chooses
precisely the loci $Y_i$ defined in \eqref{app:ss:eq:Yi}:
the cone of the morphism $i_h^*\mathcal F(-1)[-2]\to i_h^!\mathcal F$
defined in \eqref{EQ:derived-gysin-map}
is supported on

Outside $Y_i$ this support has dimension at most $i-2$,
by the definition of $Y_i$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Write $\Lambda_r=\mathbb{Z}/\ell^r\mathbb{Z}$ and abbreviate
\[
 A_r^a=H^{a-2}(X_{h,\overline k},\Lambda_r)(-1),\qquad
 B_r^a=H^a(X_{\overline k},\Lambda_r).
\]
For $r\geqslant2$, the coefficient sequence
\[
 0\longrightarrow\Lambda_{r-1}\xrightarrow{\ell}\Lambda_r
       \longrightarrow\Lambda_1\longrightarrow0
\]
gives long exact sequences compatible with the Gysin maps,
by standard properties of derived tensor products with respect to distinguished triangles
in the derived category of $\Lambda_r$-modules.
To prove the statement of Lemma~\ref{app:ss:lem:coefficients} for $\mathbb{Z}/\ell^r\mathbb{Z}$,
we induct on $r\geqslant 1$.
The case $r=1$ is precisely our assumption,
so assume that $r\geqslant 2$ and the statement already holds for $r-1$.
For $a>t$, we obtain a commutative diagram that is exact on its horizontal arrows:
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=small]
 A_1^{a-1}\arrow[r]\arrow[d]
 & A_{r-1}^{a}\arrow[r]\arrow[d]
 & A_r^a\arrow[r]\arrow[d]
 & A_1^a\arrow[r]\arrow[d]
 & A_{r-1}^{a+1}\arrow[d]\\
 B_1^{a-1}\arrow[r]
 & B_{r-1}^{a}\arrow[r]
 & B_r^a\arrow[r]
 & B_1^a\arrow[r]
 & B_{r-1}^{a+1}.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
The first vertical map is surjective, and the second, fourth, and
fifth are isomorphisms. By the five lemma the middle map is thus an
isomorphism.
For $a=t$, the last four terms instead give surjectivity
of the middle map:
the maps on $A_{r-1}^t$ and $A_1^t$ are surjective,
and the map on $A_{r-1}^{t+1}$ is injective,
so the map on $A_r^t$ is surjective by the four lemma.

Since the finite-coefficient cohomology groups are finite, the inverse
systems of kernels of the surjective maps $G_h^t(\Lambda_r)$ satisfy
the Mittag--Leffler condition. Taking inverse limits therefore preserves
surjectivity at $a=t$, as well as the isomorphisms for $a>t$.
Now $H^b(Z,\mathbb{Z}_\ell)=\varprojlim_r H^b(Z,\Lambda_r)$,
                           
giving the assertions for $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$.
Finally, the identity
$H^b(Z,\mathbb{Q}_\ell)=H^b(Z,\mathbb{Z}_\ell)\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_\ell}\mathbb{Q}_\ell$
and the flatness of $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$ over $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$
lead to the result for $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$.

label: app:ss:lem:fibre-jump
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{app:ss:lem:fibre-jump} 

Let $f:A\to B$ be a proper dominant morphism of integral varieties, and
put $c=\dim A-\dim B$. For $1\leqslant j\leqslant \dim B$, the closed locus
\[
 E_j=\{b\in B:\dim A_{\overline b}\geqslant c+j\}
\]
has codimension at least $j+1$ in $B$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This is trivial if $E_j=\emptyset$, so assume $E_j\ne \emptyset$.
The generic fibre dimension is $c$, so $E_j$ is a proper closed subset of $B$,
since $j\geqslant 1$.
Since $f$ is dominant, $f^{-1}(E_j)$ is a proper closed subset of $A$.
Since $A$ is integral,
$$\dim f^{-1}(E_j) \leqslant \dim A - 1 = \dim B + c-1.$$
However, for any irreducible component $E$ of $E_j$, some component of
$f^{-1}(E)$ dominating $E$ has dimension at least $\dim E+c+j$.
Thus $\dim f^{-1}(E_j) \geqslant \dim E_j+c+j$.
It follows that $\dim E_j \leqslant \dim B - j-1$, as desired.

label: app:ss:lem:dual-rational
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{app:ss:lem:dual-rational}
Let $V\subsetneq\operatorname{\mathbb{P}}^m_\mathbb{Q}$ be integral, but not necessarily geometrically
integral. If $V(\mathbb{Q})=\emptyset$, then
\[
 V^\vee(\mathbb{Q})\subset\operatorname{Sing}(V^\vee)(\mathbb{Q}).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that $h\in(V^\vee)_{\mathrm{sm}}(\mathbb{Q})$.
                                                                                                                                                             
The annihilator
\[
 (\mathbb T_hV^\vee)^\perp\subset\operatorname{\mathbb{P}}^m_\mathbb{Q}
\]
of the embedded tangent space is a projective linear space over $\mathbb{Q}$
of dimension $m-\dim V^\vee-1\geqslant0$. By biduality it is the fibre
over $h$ of $\mathcal N_V\to V^\vee$, viewed in the first factor,
and is therefore contained in $V$. It has a rational point,
contrary to the hypothesis $V(\mathbb{Q})=\emptyset$.

label: app:ss:prop:rational-projective
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The projection $\Sigma_\alpha\to V_\alpha^\vee$ has generic relative
dimension $c_\alpha=n-2-\dim V_\alpha^\vee$. Put
\[
 E_{\alpha,i}=\{h\in V_\alpha^\vee:
                       \dim(\Sigma_\alpha)_{\overline h}\geqslant i-1\}.
\]
Then $Y_i=\bigcup_\alpha E_{\alpha,i}$. We distinguish three cases.

If $c_\alpha>i-1$, then
$\dim V_\alpha^\vee=n-2-c_\alpha\leqslant n-i-2$, and the same bound
holds for $\overline{E_{\alpha,i}(\mathbb{Q})}$.

If $c_\alpha<i-1$, Lemma~\ref{app:ss:lem:fibre-jump} with
$1\leqslant j=i-1-c_\alpha\leqslant n-2-c_\alpha=\dim V_\alpha^\vee$ gives
\[
 \dim E_{\alpha,i}
 \leqslant\dim V_\alpha^\vee-(i-1-c_\alpha)-1=n-i-2.
\]

If $c_\alpha=i-1$, then $\dim V_\alpha^\vee=n-i-1$.
Since $V_\alpha\subset X$ has no rational point,
Lemma~\ref{app:ss:lem:dual-rational} implies that $V_\alpha^\vee(\mathbb{Q})$ lies in the proper
closed subset $\operatorname{Sing}(V_\alpha^\vee)$, of dimension at most $n-i-2$.
The closure of $E_{\alpha,i}(\mathbb{Q})$ satisfies the same bound.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $1\leqslant i\leqslant n-1$ and assume $X(\mathbb{Q})=\emptyset$.
Every nonzero $\mathbb{Q}$-point of $\mathcal Z_i$ projects to a $\mathbb{Q}$-point of $Y_i$.
Thus $\overline{\mathcal Z_i(\mathbb{Q})}$ lies in the affine cone over $\overline{Y_i(\mathbb{Q})}$,
so $\dim \overline{\mathcal Z_i(\mathbb{Q})} \leqslant 1 + \dim \overline{Y_i(\mathbb{Q})}
\leqslant n-i-1$ by Proposition~\ref{app:ss:prop:rational-projective}.
This proves \eqref{eq:rational-main}.
